text:
Lesson two. Before any tips exist, you need verified identity, because verified identity is the prerequisite for everything the trust funnel does later. When a creator signs up they prove they are a real human with a World ID orb check, and that proof shows up as a badge on their page.

Why does this matter? Because a tip is a bet on a person, not on content. If the supporter cannot tell a human from a bot farm, the first tip never happens. Verified identity contrasts with anonymous tipping pages, the kind where anyone can spin up a page in thirty seconds. Anonymous pages convert at launch and die within a month, because the trust never compounds.

Now the caveat, and I have watched this burn people. Verification adds friction, and friction at signup costs you roughly twenty percent of creators who would otherwise finish onboarding. That is real. But the creators who churn at verification were going to churn at payout setup anyway, which is a worse place to lose them. So you accept the drop at the door.

What this changes about how you build: do not bolt verification on later as a feature flag. Identity has to be the first screen, because every downstream concept, the attention page, the first tip, the supporter loop, is derived from the badge being real.
